Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 5) demonstrates a markedly enlarged, globular cardiac silhouette with a distinct radiolucent line outlining the upper mediastinum and left heart border (indicated by arrows), which represents epicardial fat separated from the pericardial fluid by the pericardium. This finding, known as the "varying cardiac density sign" or Oreo cookie sign on CT (seen in Figure 1b), is characteristic of haemopericardium or large pericardial effusion.
